facts.value: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 (doc 11829). Reported to West of England Mayoral Combined Authority Audit Committee on 6 July 2026. Prepared under the CIPFA Treasury Code, covering performance to 31 March 2026. Six appendices: Prudential Indicators (App 1), Investment Position (App 2), External Borrowing Position (App 3, but presented as a set of three funding-source and credit-rating charts since there is no borrowing), Arlingclose economic review (App 4), Interest & Capital Financing budget monitoring (App 5), and a Fitch credit-ratings glossary (App 6). Author: Steve Finnegan. Signed off by the Director of Finance, Investment & Commercial (S73 Officer) — not named in the paper. Adviser: Arlingclose.

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — WECA Audit Committee, 6 July 2026

facts.note: The MCA's finance officer is styled S73 (Local Democracy, Economic Development and Construction Act 2009) rather than S151 — the Combined Authority statutory equivalent. Steve Finnegan is the report author with a published email; the S73 Officer is not named in the paper.

facts.value: Total treasury investments £452.61m at 31 March 2026, down £9.65m from £462.26m at 31 March 2025. Weighted portfolio return 4.6% against a 4.2% average SONIA benchmark (Appendix 4 gives the 12-month SONIA average more precisely as 4.01%). Gross interest earned across all investments April 2025 to March 2026 £22.9m (Appendix 5 line: £22.931m total). MCA activities alone £22.260m against a £15.094m budget — favourable variance of £7.166m. Revolving Infrastructure Fund income £0.671m against £0.580m budget — favourable £0.091m. Total average net positive cash balance during the year £494m.

source.title: MCA Treasury Outturn 2025/26 §2.1, §2.3, §2.5, Appendix 2 Table 1 and Appendix 5

facts.note: Paragraph numbering in the paper skips §2.6 and §2.12 (minor internal quirk). §2.5 rounds MCA-activity income to £22.3m; Appendix 5 gives the exact £22.260m — same figure. The £15,094 shown at §8 finance implications is thousands (£15.094m), not '£15,094m' as printed.

facts.value: Table 1 (Appendix 2, page 2) — 31 March 2026 balances and weighted average rates: Banks & building societies (unsecured) £4.2m at 2.0% (down from £10.0m at 31 March 2025); Government (incl. local authorities) £360.0m at 4.7% (up from £351.0m); Registered Providers £10.0m at 4.8% (unchanged); Money Market Funds £26.4m at 4.0% (down from £39.3m); Social Housing REIT £5.0m at 3.2% (unchanged); pooled funds — CCLA Property £10.0m at 4.3%, Investec £10.0m at 4.2%, Kames £10.0m at 5.3%, Threadneedle £3.5m at 5.4%, M&G £3.5m at 5.9%, Royal London Enhanced Cash Plus £10.0m at 4.1%. Total £452.6m at weighted 4.6%.
facts.note: Sub-buckets sum to £452.6m to the pound. Weighted rate rebuilds to 4.62% (within one basis point of the printed 4.6%). Net movement −£9.7m ties (−5.8 + 9.0 + 0 − 12.9 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = −9.7). Note §2.8 headline of £374.2m 'diversified across UK Banks and Local Authorities' includes the £10m Reg Providers on top of £4.2m banks + £360m Gov/LA; taken as those three lines it adds correctly.

facts.value: Table 2 (Appendix 2, page 10) — 31 March 2026 balances by term: instant access notice funds £30.65m; up to 1 month £50.0m; 1-3 months £105.0m; 4-6 months £75.0m; 6-12 months £120.0m; more than 12 months £20.0m; pooled funds £51.957m. Total £452.607m. Notice period on pooled funds four days except property fund (90 days).
facts.note: Adds to £452.607m to the pound. £380.65m (84% of the book excluding pooled funds) is repricing inside 12 months — this is what drives the tight interest-rate exposure indicator against a 1% fall.

facts.value: Table 3 (Appendix 2, page 10) at 31 March 2026 — original purchase £51.956m against fair value £47.949m: net unrealised capital loss £4.007m (−7.7% of cost). In-year income return 4.61%. Individual funds: CCLA Property £9.956m → £8.856m (−£1.100m, income 4.30%); Ninety One Diversified Income (Investec) £10.000m → £9.018m (−£0.982m, 4.15%); Aegon Diversified Monthly Income (Kames) £10.000m → £9.576m (−£0.424m, 5.29%); Threadneedle Strategic Bond £3.500m → £3.121m (−£0.379m, 5.37%); M&G UK Income Distribution £3.500m → £4.123m (+£0.623m, 5.89%); Royal London Short Term Enhanced Cash £10.000m → £10.207m (+£0.207m, 4.05%); Fundamentum Social Housing REIT £5.000m → £3.048m (−£1.952m, 3.21%).
facts.note: Table arithmetic ties: purchases sum to £51,956k; fair values sum to £47,949k; capital movements sum to −£4,007k. Weighted income return 4.61% (printed). Fundamentum Social Housing REIT sits 39% below cost — the deepest single unrealised loss in the pool, on the smallest position. CCLA Property Fund down 11%. This crystallises through profit and loss unless the statutory override applies (see next fact).

facts.value: Paragraph 3 (page 6) verbatim: 'The Mayoral Combined Authority does not currently have any underlying need to borrow long term to fund capital expenditure. As part of it's approach to liquidity management, the Mayoral Combined Authority may borrow short term loans to cover any unplanned cash flow shortages as they arrive. As at 31st March 2026 the Mayoral Combined Authority held no loans.' Appendix 3 confirms no external borrowing position to report — the appendix presents only three charts of investment funding source and credit-rating splits.
facts.note: Zero external debt confirmed by Appendix 1 point 2 (Liquidity indicator): 'Total sum borrowed in past 3 months without prior notice £40m limit, £0m actual'. Appendix 5 also shows Debit Costs (Borrowing) budget £0 / outturn £0. Unusual for a Mayoral Combined Authority — GMCA, WMCA, TVCA and NECA all carry material PWLB. WoE MCA sits purely on the investor side.

facts.value: Appendix 1 point 3 (Interest Rate Exposure indicator, page 8) — upper limit on one-year revenue impact of a 1% fall in interest rates £2m; actual £1.97m. Utilisation 98.5%. The limit is set to control exposure to rate risk; the actual is close to but within limit.
facts.note: Consistent with a book that has £380.65m (84% ex-pooled) repricing inside 12 months at floating and short-dated rates. The £1.97m is the flip side of the £7.166m favourable variance in Appendix 5 — you cannot outperform benchmark this hard on a short book without carrying the equivalent downside sensitivity into the following year. Paper does not disclose the upper-limit on a 1% RISE (only the fall is given), which is a minor disclosure quirk (Appendix 1 point 3 heading mentions both but the table only prints the fall).

facts.value: Appendix 1 point 4 (Principal sums invested beyond 364 days as % of total cash balance): 2025/26 target 50% / actual 14%; 2026/27 target 30% / actual 14%; 2027/28 target 20% / actual 11%; +3 years target 20% / actual 11%. Long-term investments over three years comprise strategic pooled funds and REITs with no fixed maturity.
facts.note: All well within limit. 14% of £452.6m ≈ £63m of the book is beyond 364 days — Table 2 shows £20m 'more than 12 months' + £51.957m pooled funds = £71.957m. There is a small definitional gap between the £63m implied by the 14% indicator and the £72m Table 2 total; likely explained by the notice-availability of the pooled funds (four days for most, 90 days for CCLA Property) not counting them as beyond 364-day commitments. Not raised in the email; noted internally.

facts.value: §2.15 (page 5): 'Further to consultations in April 2023 and December 2024 MHCLG wrote to finance directors in England in February 2025 regarding the statutory override on accounting for gains and losses in pooled investment funds. On the assumption that when published regulations follow this policy announcement, the statutory override will be extended up until the 1st April 2029 for investments already in place before 1st April 2024. The override will not apply to any new investments taken out on or after 1st April 2024. The Mayoral Combined Authority had set up a reserve of £5m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended. In view of the fact that the override may not be extended past 2029 the Mayoral Combined authority has decided to maintain this reserve.'
facts.note: Relevant because £4.007m of unrealised capital loss on pooled funds currently sits behind the override, which per this statement is extended to 1 April 2029 for pre-1/4/24 investments (all seven pooled funds pre-date that cut-off). The £5m reserve is dimensioned close to the actual £4m loss — considered prudent. The override end date is a genuine 2028/29-cycle risk to the General Fund if losses remain unrecovered.

facts.value: Arlingclose economic review at Appendix 4 (page 14): 'Following the March MPC meeting, Arlingclose, the authority's treasury adviser, revised its central interest rate view and now predicts Bank Rate will be held at 3.75%.' Also from Appendix 4: 10-year gilt yield 4.65% at start of year, 4.86% at end (low 4.23%, high 4.95% within a month); 20-year gilt 5.18% → 5.45% (range 4.92%-5.55%); 12-month SONIA average 4.01%; Bank Rate cut path over 2025/26 was 4.50% → 4.25% (May) → 4.00% (Aug) → 3.75% (Dec), held in Feb and March 2026 MPC meetings.

source.title: MCA Treasury Outturn 2025/26 Appendix 4 (Arlingclose Economic & Market Review)

facts.note: Bank Rate is still 3.75% at 16 August 2026 — the Arlingclose call has held five months on. Most councils' March 2026-vintage papers assumed further cuts (Blaenau Gwent's paper had MUFG predicting cuts to 3.50% by Q2 2026 and 3.25% by Q4 2026); WoE and its adviser had a straighter read of the war-driven MPC shift. Worth naming.

facts.value: §2.14 (page 5): 'Following the reduction in Bank rates during 2025-26, the Mayoral Combined Authority will expect to receive lower income (3.75% to 4.00% from its cash and short-dated investments, including money market funds in 2026/27).' The paper does not print a 2026/27 income budget or a five-year table.
facts.note: Implicit assumption is Bank Rate holds at 3.75% (adviser call at Appendix 4). Absence of a 2026/27 income budget figure and a forward multi-year table is a schema gap that would need to be filled from the 2026/27 Treasury Strategy Statement (not in our library).

summary.text:
Mayoral Combined Authority, purely on the investor side. Paragraph 3 states 'the Mayoral Combined Authority does not currently have any underlying need to borrow long term to fund capital expenditure... As at 31st March 2026 the Mayoral Combined Authority held no loans.' Our PWLB price book returns no borrower on any variant of the name. Both sides tie to zero — a rare unqualified reconciliation, and unusual for a Mayoral Combined Authority given GMCA, WMCA, TVCA, NECA and SYMCA all carry material PWLB.

The book is £452.61m at 31 March 2026 (down £9.65m from £462.26m a year earlier) earning a weighted 4.6% against a 4.2% SONIA benchmark. Appendix 5 shows treasury income of £22.260m for the MCA against a £15.094m budget — a favourable variance of £7.166m (+47%). Table 1 arithmetic rebuilds to the pound (£4.2m banks + £360m Government/LAs + £10m Registered Providers + £26.4m MMFs + £5m Social Housing REIT + £47m other pooled = £452.6m) and the weighted rate rebuilds to 4.62% within a basis point of print.

The single most distinctive figure is on that Government/LAs line. £360m sitting at a weighted 4.7% — including counterparties, gilts and DMADF, but on Chart 3 also including LA lending — puts the MCA on the lender side of the intra-LA market at a scale we have not seen from a Combined Authority. Table 2 shows £380.65m (84% of the book excluding pooled funds) repricing inside 12 months at short-dated and floating rates. That book earned the £7.166m surplus; the flip side is the interest-rate exposure indicator at Appendix 1 point 3 — £1.97m against a £2m limit for a 1% fall in rates, 98.5% of the ceiling used.

Two dated calls in the paper worth flagging. §2.14 tells the Committee to expect 3.75%-4.00% income in 2026/27 (implicitly Bank Rate held); Arlingclose's Appendix 4 review says explicitly 'Bank Rate will be held at 3.75%'. Five months on, Bank Rate is still 3.75%. Most councils' March 2026-vintage papers assumed further cuts; the MCA and its adviser had a straighter read of the war-driven MPC shift. §2.15 covers the statutory override extension to 1 April 2029 for pre-1/4/24 pooled investments — relevant because Table 3 shows a £4.007m net unrealised capital loss (7.7% of cost) on £51.956m of pooled funds, with Fundamentum Social Housing REIT 39% below cost and CCLA Property 11% below. The £5m mitigation reserve is calibrated close to the current £4m loss.

The full balance-sheet identity (CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing) is not possible because CFR is not printed in this outturn paper (it would sit in the separate 2025/26 Strategy Statement). External borrowing = 0 is verified. What we can check inside the paper reconciles cleanly.

Steve Finnegan is the Report Author with a published email address; the S73 Officer (Combined Authority statutory equivalent of S151) is not named anywhere in the paper. The email is drafted and addressed to Steve as Report Author only, with no title attributed beyond that.

officer.body:
Hi Steve,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the Treasury Management Outturn Report that went to Audit Committee on 6 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The paper reconciles cleanly on the checks we always run first, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A cross-check first, which comes out unusually clean on both sides. Our PWLB price book returns no borrower on any variant of the MCA name; paragraph 3 of the paper confirms 'the Mayoral Combined Authority... held no loans' at 31 March 2026. Table 1 in Appendix 2 also ties — the sub-buckets sum to the £452.61m headline to the pound and the weighted rate rebuilds to 4.62% within a basis point of your printed 4.6%. Appendix 5 income totals tie too: £22.260m MCA + £0.671m RIF = £22.931m gross, variance £7.166m + £0.091m = £7.257m favourable. Nothing to raise; useful only as an honest starting point.

One data point from the paper that reads as a testable assumption — and has been proved right so far. §2.14 tells the Committee to expect 3.75%-4.00% income in 2026/27; Appendix 4 puts it more directly in Arlingclose's words: 'Bank Rate will be held at 3.75%'. Bank Rate is still 3.75% today, five months on. Most of the March 2026-vintage papers we've read this cycle assumed further cuts through Q2 and Q3 — you and your adviser had a straighter read of the war-driven MPC shift than the sector average. Worth naming.

Where the platform might be genuinely useful is on the lender side. The £360m 'Government (incl. local authorities)' line in Table 1 at a weighted 4.7% is the largest single such position we have seen in a Combined Authority paper. Chart 3 in Appendix 3 lumps £370m into 'Other Local Authorities/Gov/HA', so we cannot see from the print alone what share is DMADF or gilts versus actual LA counterparties — but at any share, the MCA sits meaningfully on the LA side of a market that most councils only see their own trades in. We track intra-LA lending across the library, so what other authorities are actually paying and offering for one-month, three-month, six-month and one-year money is visible rather than inferred. For context, July's PWLB drawings were £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin month, which shapes the deposit rates you're likely to be offered next. That sector breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

The prudential position that goes with a floating-rate book: the interest-rate exposure indicator at Appendix 1 point 3 shows £1.97m against a £2m limit for a 1% fall in rates — 98.5% of the ceiling used. It is within limit; it is close to it. That is the flip side of the favourable variance you have just booked — you cannot outperform benchmark this hard on a book with £381m repricing inside 12 months (Table 2) without carrying the equivalent downside sensitivity into the next year. Members may want to see the same indicator re-run against the 2026/27 income view when the mid-year update lands, and the live PWLB curve and SONIA path that sit behind it are on the daily dashboard at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard.

On training, five sit close to the paper. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets speaks directly to your £360m Gov/LA line. Investment strategy for debt-free councils covers the wider position. Working with treasury advisers is where the Arlingclose Bank Rate view is best tested. Prudential Code and treasury indicators covers the £1.97m/£2m discussion. Pooled funds and the statutory override matters given the £4.007m unrealised capital loss in Table 3 (Fundamentum REIT at 39% below cost, CCLA Property at 11%) and the extension timeline you set out at §2.15.
